item.title: Chinese peacekeepers to South Sudan (Juba) participate in force commanders' exchange meeting
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
By Lu Jinfang, Wang Shuai, LyuJunqi, Yang Shiwei, Zhou Fei and Wang Liguo JUBA, Nov. 16 -- The United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) recently convened a force commanders' conference and on-site exchange demonstration. The 12th Chinese Peacekeeping Infantry Battalion to UNMISS participated in the event. Focusing on comprehensive defense, Chinese peacekeepers joined forces with the United Nations Police (UNPOL) and the Nepal Armed Police Force (APF) to conduct an emergency response exercise for an influx of displaced people as well as an emergency combat assault demonstration, showcasing its rapid and efficient emergency response capabilities to all participating parties. Participants also visited the Chinese camp for an on-site observation, gaining a detailed understanding of Chinese peacekeepers' daily combat readiness management, duty system operations, and comprehensive defense system construction. (Video Editor: Liu Sen)

item.title: China Coast Guard ship Sandu concludes visit to Malaysia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16--The China Coast Guard (CCG) ship Sandu (Hull 5308) concluded its four-day friendly visit to Penang, Malaysia, on November 13, and set sail for home. During the transit, vessels from China and Malaysia conducted maritime formation training and a communications exercise. In the formation training, the CCG ship Sandu and the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) ship KM Tun Fatimah (Hull 8305) shifted between column and line-abreast formations. During the visit, the Chinese and Malaysian sides held high-level meetings and conducted multiple training subjects, including a maritime search and rescue tabletop exercise, formation training, and a communications exercise. The two sides also hosted activities such as open-ship days, cultural and sports exchanges, and a deck receptionevent. (Video Editor: Yang Xueqing)

item.title: Xi to hold China-Russia-U.S. summit with Putin, Trump
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in China's Shenzhen on Nov. 19, 2026, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Monday.

item.title: Acts of Japanese right-wing forces blatantly challenge postwar international order: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 -- "The international community needs to stay highly vigilant and take countermeasures against Japan's push for remilitarization, uphold the international nuclear non-proliferation regime, and defend security and peace of the world," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a regular press briefing on Friday. It's reported that Japan will continue to label China as its greatest strategic challenge in its revised three security documents, and increase its defense spending to 70 to 80 trillion yen over the next five years. The Japanese government is considering amending its National Security Strategy to include exceptions to the three non-nuclear principles, which potentially allows the transport of nuclear weapons into Japan in emergencies. When being asked to comment on the reports, the spokesperson first pointed out that Japan is a defeated country in WWII. Looking back, Japanese militarists committed heinous crimes, inflicting untold suffering on people in the Asia-Pacific and beyond. He then emphasized that the Japanese side should have reflected on its history of aggression and war crimes, and drawn lessons from history. Instead, right-wing forces in Japan keep fabricating false narratives on the so-called China threat, and distorting facts to portray Japan as a victim. The spokesperson also noted that at the same time, they are ramping up defense expenditure, strengthening offensive and long-range strike capabilities, and, worse still, seeking to progressively ease nuclear restrictions. "With such moves, they have not only betrayed Japan's commitment to peace, but also blatantly challenged the postwar international order and the authority of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons," stressed the spokesperson.

item.title: The Philippines Should Rein in Dangerous Words and Actions of Certain Politicians: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13-- "Driven by political prejudice and self-interest, certain Filipino politicians made remarks which run counter to the solemn commitment the Philippine government has made to China on the Taiwan question. We strongly deplore and firmly oppose such statements," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's defense ministry, at a press briefing on Friday. According to reports, the Philippine Defense Secretary said in a recent interview that with 200,000 Filipinos residing in Taiwan, the Philippines is preparing for all contingencies, and that it would be counterproductive for China to try to seize Taiwan by force. In response to that, thespokesperson noted that the Taiwan question is purely China's internal affair. How to resolve it is a matter for the Chinese people, which brooks no foreign interference. The spokesperson also emphasized that China is firm in its resolve to safeguard sovereignty and territorial integrity and achieve national reunification. "We urges the Philippine side to rein in the dangerous words and actions of these politicians, abide by the one-China principle, and take real actions to maintain stable China-Philippines relations," stressed the spokesperson.
